title: A meeting link taken from an event's free-text description/location carries no provenance marker and flows into auto-join unchanged: an outsider's invite can make every-webinar mode join and record an arbitrary meeting
area: apps/api/src/gws-calendar.ts:159-168 (link.source computed by resolveEventMeetingLink but dropped at the mapper); packages/meeting-bot/src/calendar/auto-join.ts:78 (calendar organizer => senderVerified true) and :190; schedule-tick.ts:203 (production everyWebinar:true)
evidence: Probe on 9bc316c: resolveEventMeetingLink({description:'Join our Webinar: https://zoom.us/j/123456789?pwd=zz'}) -> {url,source:'description'}; the mapped UpcomingMeeting has meetingUrl but NO source key (source is discarded). Fed to selectAutoRecordItems as a CalendarEvent {title:'Free Webinar: Win a prize', organizer:'attacker@evil.com'}: everyWebinar:true -> toSchedule length 1, skipped []; everyWebinar:false -> untrusted-sender. The same event without the extracted link (pre-change shape) -> skipped no-join-link. So events that could not be joined before (outsider invites carry the link in LOCATION/DESCRIPTION, not conferenceData) are now recorded in production mode with no check; the Gmail side requires an authenticated sender (D-122 ruling 1) or approval, the Calendar side now has neither and no way to tell the link came from free text.
fix_direction: Cycle 1 minimum: map a typed field meetingUrlSource: 'conference'|'location'|'description' onto UpcomingMeeting (type in routes/calendar.ts) from link.source (absent only when no meetingUrl); test it in the mapper and over HTTP; manifest states that location/description links must not be auto-joined without the Gmail-equivalent trust gate; and a safe default: either the scheduler loader ignores non-conference sources until a policy unit says otherwise, or free-text links are returned under a separate non-joinable field. Today's code default is the opposite: joinable.

title: Manifest says the join path applies hasEmbeddedRedirect downstream; it does not: the auto-join path never calls it, so the mirror accepts redirect-carrying links the canonical planner refuses
area: apps/api/src/join-rules/calendar-link-extract.ts recognise(); packages/meeting-bot/src/send-now.ts:76,166 (only planSendNow, whose only caller is send-now-command.ts); auto-record-policy.ts:100 webinarIdentity checks only https + detectPlatform
evidence: Differential over 1315 constructed URLs (121 accepted by both, identities identical in all 121): 42 accepted by the mirror and refused by planSendNow, 38 embedded-redirect, e.g. https://zoom.us/j/12345678901?redirect=https://evil.com , ?url=//evil.com , ?next=%2f%2fevil.com , ?x=https%3A%2F%2Fevil.com , ?x=%2568ttps%253A%252F%252Fevil.com ; the rest 'https:/zoom.us/j/12345678901' (href form, normalised by URL). grep: planSendNow/hasEmbeddedRedirect have no caller on the schedule-tick path.
fix_direction: Mirror hasEmbeddedRedirect (REDIRECT_KEY, URL_VALUE, up to 3 decodeAll) in the extractor with those URLs as a standing refusal corpus, and correct the manifest sentence.

title: Same meeting written twice: the first variant wins, so a passcode-less copy listed before the pwd copy drops the passcode and the bot cannot join
area: apps/api/src/join-rules/calendar-link-extract.ts scan() dedupe (!res.joins.some(j => j.id === r.id)); the test pins 'first URL kept' only for two variants that both carry pwd
evidence: resolveEventMeetingLink({description:'https://zoom.us/j/999999999 and https://zoom.us/j/999999999?pwd=SECRET'}) -> url 'https://zoom.us/j/999999999'; reversed order -> '...?pwd=SECRET'. Deterministic but order-dependent. pwd=A vs pwd=B -> A (first).
fix_direction: On an identity collision keep the variant that carries a passcode parameter, else the first; test both orders.

title: Second recogniser list has no differential test: the drift guard cannot catch host-list or path-rule divergence from platform.ts/send-now.ts
evidence: Mutations on the copy that pass extractor (14) and calendar (14) tests: M10a add host zoomgov.com to the zoom list (canonical detectPlatform refuses it) -> SURVIVED; M15 webex rule h.endsWith('webex.com') (accepts evilwebex.com) -> SURVIVED. The guard checks only that every canonical host is accepted by the copy (recall direction), not that the copy accepts nothing more.
fix_direction: Add a differential test over a shared corpus (hosts x paths x schemes, accepted and hostile) importing detectPlatform/meetingIdentity/planSendNow from packages/meeting-bot (tests may cross packages), asserting copy-join implies canonical-join with identical identity; or move the recognisers to packages/core first.

title: Zoom host START links (/s/<id>?zak=...) are accepted from free text and returned in meetingUrl with the host token
area: apps/api/src/join-rules/calendar-link-extract.ts zoom regex (?:j|w|s|wc/join); no test pins /s/ either way (mutation M14 removing /s/ SURVIVED)
evidence: resolveEventMeetingLink({description:'https://zoom.us/s/12345678901?zak=TOKEN'}) -> {url:'https://zoom.us/s/12345678901?zak=TOKEN',source:'description'}. The canonical extractor also accepts /s/ (parity), but a calendar-text link is where a start-as-host URL and its zak credential reach the scheduler and the API response.
fix_direction: Refuse /s/ and any zak= parameter in the calendar extractor, with a test; leave the canonical recogniser to a separate decision.
